findings.F1: In the falling calm profile the run-break fade lasts beyond the tested day. After an up close ending 2 or more down closes, the short-signed excess return is +0.92 % at 1 day (t 2.22, 258 cases, 152 days), +1.35 % at 2 days (t 2.23, 150 days) and +1.38 % at 3 days (t 1.73). On a non-overlapping 3-day grid the 3-day reading rises to +2.56 % (t 2.15, 103 cases, 58 days). That is about 2.5 times the 1-day move, against the same 0.19 % cost per trade.
findings.F2: Among all run-breaks with 2 or more down closes, the fade is convex in the run's depth scaled by the 30-day swing. The bottom three depth quartiles give next-day short excess of −0.05 %, +0.88 % and +0.35 % (t ≤ 1.7). The deepest quartile gives +2.11 % (t 4.16, 216 cases, 99 days). The convex deep-run fade in falling markets is already held (074-01.b1.g1).
findings.F3: The fade is absent in rising markets, as the brief predicts. There the 1-, 2-, 3- and 5-day short excess is −0.39 %, −0.67 %, −0.31 % and −0.33 % (t from −0.24 to −0.80, 176 cases, 98 days), and the deep half is −0.40 % at 1 day.
findings.F4: The fade also appears in choppy markets (60-day return between −10 % and +10 %), and grows with the horizon. The short excess is +1.26 % at 1 day (t 1.78), +2.36 % at 3 days (t 2.37) and +3.42 % at 5 days (t 2.78), over 77 to 81 cases on 61 to 65 days.
findings.F5: The choppy fade is graded by depth. The deep half gives +3.49 % over 3 days (t 2.11, 40 cases, 35 days) against +1.16 % for the shallow half (t 1.17), and the 3-day slope on depth is +0.0133 (Spearman 0.12).
findings.F6: Part of the choppy fade is drift. Every choppy day taken short on a 3-day grid already gives +1.34 % excess (t 1.70, 212 cases). The choppy run-break on the 3-day grid is +1.79 % (t 1.32, 31 cases), so the gain over the profile's base rate is only about 1 point on few independent cases.
findings.F7: In falling agitated markets the deep half of run-breaks gives +3.43 % the next day (t 3.43) and +5.86 % over 3 days (t 3.40, 33 cases, 24 days), with Spearman 0.33 on depth. This cell is already held by 074-01.b1.d1.d1 and 074-01.b1.g1 (falling, short).
findings.F8: The tested book's cases are concentrated in one year. 2018 gives +1.79 % next-day short excess (t 2.46, 120 cases), while 2019, 2020 and 2021 give +0.23 %, +0.18 % and +0.11 % (all t < 0.5). This fits its Calmar of 0.23 and its Sharpe falling short of holding's.
findings.F9: Other angles stood out from chance only weakly or repeat what is held:

ideas.idea: In a falling, calm market, the first up day after a run of down days is followed by a fall in the coin's close over the next three days. The deeper the run's fall against the coin's usual daily swing over the last 30 days, the larger that three-day fall.
ideas.consequence: A trader shorting relief days in a quiet downtrend holds the short for about three days rather than one, so each trade captures several times its cost.
ideas.name: calm downtrend relief fade three days

ideas.idea: In a choppy market, the first up day after a run of down days is followed by a fall in the coin's close over the next five days. The deeper the run's fall against the coin's usual daily swing over the last 30 days, the larger that fall.
ideas.consequence: A trader in a sideways market fades the first bounce after a deep slide, in the choppy short cells where the research holds almost no short strategy.
ideas.name: choppy market relief fade
